messages:
maya: heads up — customer reported a suspicious BYOK migration event, asking if we can confirm chain-of-custody. saw an unexpected rewrap request. :eyes:
alejandro: which customer / key-id? do we have audit logs showing export vs rewrap?
sara: customer: acme-payments. key-id: cmk-afe23. attaching log snippet i pulled from the HSM proxy logs:
```
2024-08-14T15:02:03Z proxy: received rewrap request key=cmk-afe23 from svc=onprem-migrator src=10.2.4.13 request_id=aa1b2c
2024-08-14T15:02:04Z hsm: rewrap accepted session=0x7f4a auth=token-opaque actor=svc:onprem-migrator
2024-08-14T15:02:05Z audit: wrapped-key-exported id=wrap-0x9b1c size=4096 purpose=migration
```
maya: hmm, note says wrapped-key-exported — our policy forbids exportable wrapped keys for BYOK customers unless preapproved.
jess: i've opened INC-402 and notified compliance. tagging @rowan for RBAC look. please add any quick containment steps in the thread. :lock:
rowan: quick questions — did the proxy authenticate with a service principal or an operator user? logs show actor=svc:onprem-migrator. that implies a service principal token, not a human. who owns that SP?
alejandro: looks like svc:onprem-migrator belongs to infra-team-runbooks. i can ping infra and ask to suspend the SP temporarily.
sara: also note the auth token used appears to be short-lived but rewrap was allowed because the SP had role kms:wrap, kms:export in the old RBAC mapping. we started the RBAC migration last week; maybe this service missed the update.
rowan: urgent action: remove kms:export from that service principal, keep kms:wrap only (wrap without export). can we do that via the RBAC API quickly?
alejandro: yes, PATCH to /rbac/principals/svc:onprem-migrator with body: `{ "remove": ["kms:export"] }` — i'll stage it to prod in 5m.
infra-bot: deploy job started for rbac-change svc:onprem-migrator at 2024-08-14T15:10:20Z job=rbac-patch-9921 status=queued
maya: containment: recommend immediate rotate of the ephemeral wrap key and set a deny policy on export for that CMK until evidence is reviewed. also preserve all HSM audit buffers.
jess: compliance requested chain-of-custody artifacts: audit logs, proxy config, SP credential creation events, and any SSO session logs. i've attached a checklist in INC-402.
sara: forensics note — do not restart the HSM or clear the audit buffers. snapshot the audit files to a compliant bucket with immutability flags. commands i suggest:
```
aws s3 cp /var/log/hsm/audit s3://forensics-acme/1723456789/ --recursive --acl bucket-owner-full-control
redwood kms set-policy --key cmk-afe23 --policy '{"Statement": [{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"kms:Export","Principal":"*"}]}' --force
```
rowan: while we do that, we should confirm whether wrapped-key-exported means an export to a persistent external key or merely a wrapped blob returned to the caller (allowed for migration flows when customer explicitly requested). sara, can you check the proxy code path for wrap vs export?
sara: checking now — proxy has two code paths: wrap-for-remote (returns wrapped blob), and export-entire-key (calls hsm-key-export API). the audit line 'wrapped-key-exported' is ambiguous; i can grep raw hsm debug level logs and look for hsm-key-export calls.
alejandro: if we find hsm-key-export then treat as high severity. otherwise mark P1 and continue.
maya: notify customer to pause any migration operations and ask them to provide the requestor identity. don't promise outcomes. script suggestion: "We are investigating and have temporarily paused migration while we validate key handling."
jess: done — message sent to customer contact. customer responded with a sysadmin name and time. they say migration was kicked off by their automation, not a human.
rowan: ok next steps: (1) suspend SP (alejandro) (2) snapshot audit (sara) (3) apply deny-export policy (maya/jess) (4) rotate ephemeral wrap key and create new wrap key tied to escrow workflow (infra) (5) compile COC package for compliance and legal. assign owners in INC-402.
alejandro: started suspend now. patch applied, awaiting infra-bot confirmation.
infra-bot: rbac-patch-9921 status=success effected_principal=svc:onprem-migrator removed_permissions=[kms:export] at 2024-08-14T15:12:01Z
sara: audit snapshot uploaded to s3://forensics-acme/1723456789/, checksum attached to INC-402. i've also exported raw HSM debug logs to the same bucket.
maya: good. we should also run a scoped vuln triage: check whether the proxy had a CVE that allowed privilege escalation causing export. assign to eng-runtime.
rowan: noted. tagging eng-runtime for triage. @eng-runtime please pick up CVE scan and short-lived token review.
alejandro: final ask — ensure we preserve timeline metadata: who approved any RBAC exceptions in the last 30 days. jess, can legal request the approval logs?
jess: yes, adding approval logs export to the compliance bundle.
maya: thanks team. we'll leave the incident open until export is ruled out or we complete an emergency rotation and customer signs off. :white_check_mark:
